la:other:Alcides.html:
Alcīdes, ae, m., = Ἀλκείδης,
a male descendant of Alceus; usu. his grandson Hercules, ; ; : quid memorem Alciden?; so ; ; : non fugis, Alcide,; voc. also Alcidā, .

la:other:Alcibiades.html:
Alcĭbĭădes, is, m. (
gen. Alcibiadi, ; voc. Gr. Alcibiadē, ), = Ἀλκιβιάδης.
An Athenian general in the time of the Peloponnesian war, distinguished for his beauty, wealth, and natural endowments, as well as for his changing fortunes and want of fixed principle, ; (his life, v. in Plut., Nep., and Just.).—Hence, * Alcĭbĭădēus, a, um, adj., pertaining to him, .—
The name of a later Greek in the time of the war with the Romans, .

la:other:Alcmena.html:
Alcmēna or Alcŭmēna, ae, also Alcmēnē, ēs, f. (always Alcumena in :
Alcmene,; gen., Gr. Dor. Alcumenās, Argum.; Alcmenes,), = Ἀλκμήνη, daughter of Electryon, wife of Amphitryo, and mother of Hercules by Jupiter, and of his twin-brother Iphiclus by Amphitryo, ;

la:other:Alcaeus.html:
Alcaeus, i, m., = Ἀλκαῖος,
a renowned lyric poet of Mitylene, contemporary with Sappho, 610 B.C., inventor of the metre which bears his name, and which was imitated by the Latin poets, esp. by Horace; v. ; ; ; ; ; .— Hence, Alcăĭcus, a, um, adj., = Ἀλκαϊκός, of or pertaining to Alcœus: versus, the Alcaic verse; cf. P.; Grotef. Gr. II. 107; Zumpt, Gr. § 866.
